primitives.name: Individual Perfection Impossibility
primitives.verbatim_quote: REQUIREMENTS OF THE INDIVIDUAL The attainment of individual perfection is as impossible in football as in anything else, for absolute faultlessness does not exist in the human being.
primitives.assumptions: Human performance is bounded by inherent variability and cannot achieve zero error.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At perfect performance limit, variance approaches zero, violating probabilistic model assumptions.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic model of athletic improvement where deterministic perfection is excluded.
layer2.telemetry: Athlete performance variance vs. theoretical ideal.

primitives.name: Physical Strength and Bravery
primitives.verbatim_quote: In the first place, a football player absolutely must be physically strong and rugged.
primitives.assumptions: Strength and bravery are necessary conditions for participation in football.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when either strength or bravery falls below critical threshold.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's player readiness kernel where strength and courage define viable action space.
layer2.telemetry: Player strength index and fear response measurement.

primitives.name: Training Efficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: Out of the many who can with consistent training improve their bodies, only a few will do so.
primitives.assumptions: Training efficacy follows a power-law distribution among participants.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Training efficacy drops to zero when effort or capacity is insufficient.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's efficiency function that models training impact on athlete capability.
layer2.telemetry: Improvement rate per unit time of training intensity.

The foundational structure of football's individual requirements forms a dual vector space: one axis representing physical strength and the other mental fortitude. These dimensions are not orthogonal but interact dynamically—strength alone is insufficient without courage, and vice versa. The impossibility of perfection implies that any model of athlete development must incorporate stochasticity and bounded rationality. The training efficiency primitive reveals a power-law distribution of outcomes, suggesting that while many may begin, only a minority reach elite status due to diminishing returns in effort. This creates a failure mode where marginal gains plateau, and thus, optimization strategies must account for both probabilistic improvement and resource allocation constraints. The interplay between these primitives defines a non-Euclidean performance manifold where each player's trajectory is unique yet constrained by shared physical and psychological limits.
